lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: reading an everyday agreement before signing

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic reading an everyday agreement before signing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional short agreement in full, then identifies five specific commitments it contains, such as cost, timing, cancellation terms, and any conditions the reader is easy to miss.
safetyNotes: The agreement is entirely fictional and provided with this lesson; no real business, account, or signature is involved.
materials: learner-local: the provided fictional agreement document

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Name one specific habit you could realistically build to catch easy-to-miss terms without reading every document word for word every time.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Identification of specific terms: Lists at least three specific, correct terms from the agreement. | Identifying the easy-to-miss term: Names a term that is genuinely easy to miss and gives a plausible reason. | Realistic habit-building: Proposes a specific, realistic habit for catching key terms. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner rewrite the agreement's hardest-to-find term in one plain sentence, as if explaining it to someone who hasn't read the document at all.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic reading an everyday agreement before signing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the provided fictional agreement document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: a notebook or document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

resources.title: reading an everyday agreement before signing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads a provided fictional short agreement in full, then identifies five specific commitments it contains, such as cost, timing, cancellation terms, and any conditions the reader is easy to miss.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact reading an everyday agreement before signing decision or action.
Model move 2: Before reading closely, note how you'd normally handle an agreement like this if you were in a hurry.
Model move 3: Read the full fictional agreement and identify five specific things it commits the signer to.

Model check: Identification of specific terms: Lists at least three specific, correct terms from the agreement. | Identifying the easy-to-miss term: Names a term that is genuinely easy to miss and gives a plausible reason. | Realistic habit-building: Proposes a specific, realistic habit for catching key terms.

resources.title: reading an everyday agreement before signing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for reading an everyday agreement before signing.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: reading an everyday agreement before signing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads a provided fictional short agreement in full, then identifies five specific commitments it contains, such as cost, timing, cancellation terms, and any conditions the reader is easy to miss.
Coach direction: Before reading closely, note how you'd normally handle an agreement like this if you were in a hurry.
Learner prompt: Honestly describe how much of a document like this you'd normally read before agreeing, in a real hurry-up moment.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: reading an everyday agreement before signing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read the full fictional agreement and identify five specific things it commits the signer to.
Response 1 (t2-p1): List five specific commitments the agreement contains (for example, a cost, a timing rule, a cancellation term, or a condition).
Response 2 (t2-p2): I read the entire agreement, not only the first paragraph.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: reading an everyday agreement before signing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Name one specific habit you could realistically build to catch easy-to-miss terms without reading every document word for word every time.

Success checks: Identification of specific terms: Lists at least three specific, correct terms from the agreement. | Identifying the easy-to-miss term: Names a term that is genuinely easy to miss and gives a plausible reason. | Realistic habit-building: Proposes a specific, realistic habit for catching key terms.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: reading an everyday agreement before signing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional reading an everyday agreement before signing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Identification of specific terms: Lists at least three specific, correct terms from the agreement. | Identifying the easy-to-miss term: Names a term that is genuinely easy to miss and gives a plausible reason. | Realistic habit-building: Proposes a specific, realistic habit for catching key terms..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner reads a provided fictional short agreement in full, then identifies five specific commitments it contains, such as cost, timing, cancellation terms, and any conditions the reader is easy to miss.

simulationRoute.title: reading an everyday agreement before signing — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the reading an everyday agreement before signing task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Identification of specific terms: Lists at least three specific, correct terms from the agreement. | Identifying the easy-to-miss term: Names a term that is genuinely easy to miss and gives a plausible reason. | Realistic habit-building: Proposes a specific, realistic habit for catching key terms.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
